title: Replay-driven failure simulator: customer-trace validation for circuit breakers & load-shedding
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a deterministic, trace-driven chaos harness that replays representative customer request traces while injecting region ejection, GPU pool exhaustion, and dependency blackholes. The goal is to validate that circuit breakers, admission control, and load-shedding policies keep SLOs and error budgets within acceptable bounds and that rollout/fallback logic routes traffic predictably during progressive infrastructure degradation.
background: We have ad-hoc chaos experiments for region partition and GPU saturation, but results vary because tests use synthetic traffic and nondeterministic injection timing. Product teams want confidence that policy changes (circuit breaker thresholds, admission control backoff, multi-region failover routing) behave when fed real request distributions from customers. This ticket implements a replay harness that uses sampled traces to create realistic demand patterns and exercises cascading failure scenarios deterministically.
approach: Ingest sampled production traces (sanitized) and convert into replay jobs with preserved temporal distribution and token-length characteristics.
Create scenario definitions that combine: gradual region ejection, staged GPU node drain (percent-by-pool), and downstream dependency blackhole windows (with configurable latency/failure profiles).
Coordinate injections with a central controller that can run deterministic timelines (timewarp), enabling fast-forwarded test runs and exact repeatability across clusters.

Instrument the controller to collect the same SLO telemetry as Console (p50/p95/p99 latencies, token throughput, error rate, admission/reject counts, circuit state transitions), and output a blinded comparison against baseline runs.

Add assertions that represent policy-level expectations: circuit opens only after X consecutive backend failures; admission control reduces accepted QPS before latency SLO is breached; fallback to warm region occurs within N seconds.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can replay a 24-hour sampled trace in <30 minutes using timewarp and produce deterministic metric outputs.
At least three scenario templates implemented: immediate-region-cut, progressive-gpu-drain (0->90% over 10m), and dependency-blackhole-with-latency-spikes.
Console dashboards ingest test telemetry and show differences vs baseline run automatically.
Automated assertions pass/fail reported and stored; failures create a linked GitHub issue with a reproducible harness job attached.
Runbook drafted for interpreting results and recommended policy changes (circuit thresholds, queue limits, fallback delays).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Using production traces may contain sensitive tokens. Mitigation: only use sanitized samples stored in a restricted staging bucket and apply strict redaction prior to replay.

Risk: Injecting destructive scenarios into shared clusters could impact other tests. Mitigation: run harness in dedicated staging clusters with isolated GPU pools and traffic blinds to avoid cross-impact.
Risk: Non-determinism from background autoscaling. Mitigation: pin autoscaling policies for test clusters and snapshot cluster topology at test start.
Risk: Long runtime of full traces. Mitigation: timewarp feature and trace sampling slices to produce statistically equivalent shorter runs.
implementation_notes: Controller will be a small Go binary sitting in infra/tools with a YAML-driven scenario DSL.
Trace converter reuses existing trace parsers from dashboard ingestion service; add a sampling/length-preservation module.
Integrate with existing chaos-injection library (chaos-agent) but add deterministic timeline and scheduled checkpoints for circuit-state capture.
Expose a web UI to assemble scenarios and launch repeatable runs; initial MVP is CLI-only with JSON artifacts stored in GCS.
Telemetry mapping: ensure we emit request-level tags (trace_id, model_id, region, pool_id) to enable per-tenant analysis without exposing PII.
milestones: M1: prototype controller + single scenario replay (2025-11-14)
M2: integrate deterministic timeline and GPU-drain injection (2025-11-21)
M3: console ingestion and automated assertions (2025-11-28)
M4: runbook + handoff to SRE + first policy tuning session with PMs (2025-12-03)
notes: We should avoid copying naming used in existing chaos tickets; this harness focuses on trace fidelity and determinism rather than ad-hoc stress.
Coordinate with Privacy & Legal to approve trace sampling approach before starting ingestion (task created: PRIV-134).
Reach out to Console team (owner: Lina Gomez) to add temporary collection endpoints for test telemetry ingestion.
Consider adding a follow-up ticket to run cross-tenant fairness checks under load-shedding (ensure low-priority tenants are not catastrophically starved).
